findings.title: Row Level Security is off for public.app_settings
findings.plain: Anyone who has your app's public key (it's visible in your website's code) can read, add, change and delete every row in "app_settings".
findings.fix: Turn on Row Level Security. The fix allows read-only access for now. Decide whether "app_settings" should be public at all.

findings.title: Row Level Security is off for public.profiles
findings.plain: Anyone who has your app's public key (it's visible in your website's code) can read, add, change and delete every row in "profiles".
findings.fix: Turn on Row Level Security and add rules so each user can only reach their own rows (matched on id).

findings.title: Row Level Security is off for public.subscriptions
findings.plain: Anyone who has your app's public key (it's visible in your website's code) can read, add, change and delete every row in "subscriptions".
findings.fix: Turn on Row Level Security so each user can only read their own rows. Changes to "subscriptions" should come only from your server (for example a payment webhook or an admin function).

findings.title: Secret in a public environment variable (VITE_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) found in src/config.ts:2
findings.plain: Variables that start with VITE_ are copied into your website when it's built, so anyone can read their values. Found: VITE_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
findings.fix: Treat this key as leaked: replace (rotate) it in the provider's dashboard now, delete it from the code, and move whatever needs it into a server-side function that reads it from a secret setting.

findings.title: Supabase service_role key found in src/lib/admin.ts:7
findings.plain: It's in code that runs in the browser, so anyone visiting your site can find it. Found: eyJhbGciOi… (221 characters)
findings.fix: Treat this key as leaked: replace (rotate) it in the provider's dashboard now, delete it from the code, and move whatever needs it into a server-side function that reads it from a secret setting.

findings.target: public.notes, rule "Enable insert for authenticated users only"
findings.title: Rule "Enable insert for authenticated users only" on public.notes lets users reach other users' rows
findings.plain: Any logged-in user can add rows to "notes" that claim to belong to a different user.
findings.fix: Replace this rule with one that only matches rows where user_id is the current user.

findings.target: public.notes, rule "Enable read access for all users"
findings.title: Rule "Enable read access for all users" on public.notes lets users read other users' rows
findings.plain: Anyone, even without logging in, can see every user's rows in "notes", not just their own.
findings.fix: Replace this rule with one that only matches rows where user_id is the current user.

findings.title: Users can set their own role in public.profiles
findings.plain: When a user edits their own row in "profiles", nothing stops them from also changing "role". That could let someone make themselves an admin or unlock paid features for free.
findings.fix: Allow users to edit only the safe columns of "profiles"; "role" can then only be changed by your server.

findings.title: View public.note_counts ignores Row Level Security
findings.plain: "note_counts" shows data using its creator's full permissions, so it skips your access rules. Anyone with your app's public key can read everything it shows.
findings.fix: Make the view run with the permissions of the person asking (security_invoker), so your table rules apply.

findings.title: Function public.get_all_emails exposes your users table
findings.plain: "get_all_emails" reads your users table (emails and account details) with full database permissions, and anyone, even without logging in, can call it.
findings.fix: Stop the public and logged-in users from calling it. If your app needs it, call it from a server function instead.

findings.title: Storage bucket "avatars" is public
findings.plain: Anyone with a file's link can download files in "avatars". That's fine for things like profile pictures, not for private documents.
findings.fix: If files in "avatars" are private, make the bucket private and serve files with signed links.
